bib.title: Belief Dynamics Reveal the Dual Nature of In-Context Learning and Activation Steering

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Belief Dynamics Reveal the Dual Nature of In-Context Learning and Activation Steering", Bigelow*, Wurgaft*, Wang, Goodman, Ullman, Tanaka, Lubana (Goodfire AI, Harvard, Stanford, NTT Research). arXiv 2511.00617v2, labelled "Preprint. March 13, 2026" (cs.LG, 12 Mar 2026).

COVERAGE: Text of about 146.5k chars extracted. About 114.5k remained after I dropped figure-glyph noise (lines containing "gid000", plus short axis-label fragments in the later sections). I read the whole body, discussion, appendices A-H, the figure captions and the appendix captions. The reference list I only skimmed. Figures were extracted as garbled glyphs, so I read their captions (last caption on p29) but could not see the plots. I did not run a page count; the caption list ends at p29. Heatmap and curve values are visible only in the plots, so no numbers are reported from them.

CENTRAL CLAIM: In-context examples and activation steering both change behaviour by changing the model's belief over latent concepts. ICL accumulates evidence through the likelihood term. Steering shifts the prior odds. The two add in log-odds space, which produces a phase boundary: behaviour flips suddenly at a context length that depends on the steering magnitude. One closed-form model fits all of this.

Model (Eq. 9): log o(c|x) = a*m + b + gamma*N^(1-alpha).
- N = number of shots.
- m = steering magnitude.
- a, b, gamma, alpha = four fitted scalars.
- Eq. 5 gives p(y(c)|x) = sigma(-log p(c)/p(c') - gamma*N^(1-alpha)).
- Crossover context length (Eq. 10): N*(m) = (-(a*m+b)/gamma)^(1/(1-alpha)).

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. The fitted model predicts held-out behaviour very well across context length and steering magnitude.
 number: r = 0.98, averaged over 5 domains.
 setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 5 persona datasets, 10-fold cross-validation holding out 3 adjacent steering magnitudes. Behaviour is the Yes/No token probability, averaged over 100 sampled exemplar sequences per cell.
 quote: "Overall, we find a very high correlation between LLM probabilities and predictions on held-out data (r= 0.98, averaged across our 5 domains; p < .001 for all correlations)."
 where: p4.
2. The crossover point N* is predictable.
 number: r = 0.97 (Llama). Appendix B gives r = 0.91 for Qwen-2.5-7B and r = 0.97 for Gemma-2-9B.
 quote: "The belief dynamics model is highly predictive of crossover points N ∗ between c and c′, with a correlation of r= 0.97 (p < .001)".
 where: Fig. 8 caption, p7. Appendix B, p18.
3. ICL curves are sigmoidal in N^(1-alpha), a sub-linear evidence accumulation. This is why plotting against log shots gives the "sudden learning" curve.
 number: none (functional form).
 quote: "we predict and demonstrate that in-context learning dynamics follow a sigmoid curve as a function of N 1−α."
 where: p6.
4. Steering shifts the ICL curve without changing its shape. Positive magnitudes reach the transition with fewer shots, and negative magnitudes need more.
 quote: "positive steering magnitudes lead to similar ICL dynamics with fewer in-context examples (i.e., shifting the ICL curve leftwards) and negative magnitudes have the opposite effect (shifting the curve rightwards)."
 where: p6.
5. Steering response is sigmoidal in probability (linear in log-odds) over a limited magnitude range.
 number: m in [-3,3] for the Dark Triad datasets and [-1.5,1.5] for the Moral Nihilism datasets, on Llama-3.1-8B.
 quote: "We observe this within the range m∈[−3,3] for the Dark Triad datasets, and the range m∈[−1.5,1.5] for Moral Nihilism datasets for Llama-3.1-8B."
 where: p7.
 Beyond that range the effect breaks down. quote: "behavior converges towards chance (p(y|x) = 0.5), even with very large" magnitudes (App. C, p19-22).
6. The result holds at larger scale and on other tasks.
 - Llama-3.1-70B: r = 0.98 cross-validated. quote: "(cross-validated out-of-sample r= 0.98, see Fig. 15)". Also "ICL occurs substantially faster, and the models begin to match the persona with merely a few examples" (App. D).
 - High-prior concept (openness): r = 0.87 (App. E).
 - Flipped-label financial sentiment, 3 labels: r = 0.96 (App. F). "the LLM requires substantially more shots".
7. Steering acts on the prior and is input-independent. Steering therefore changes behaviour even on inputs that do not favour the concept.
 quote: "steering yields a constant shift in the model log-posterior odds that will consistently change model beliefs for both an individual observation x or an entire population".
 where: p6.
8. Steering vectors computed from many-shot contexts, normalised to equal norm, were weaker than single-query vectors.
 quote: "counter-intuitively, after vectors were normalized to equal magnitude, steering vectors computed over multiple shots had an even weaker effect than steering with vectors computed over a single query."
 where: p8-9. App. G, Llama-3.1-8B, Psychopathy dataset.

EXPERIMENT SETUP
- Tasks: Perez et al. 2022 persona datasets, 1000 items each, "Is the following statement something you would say?" with Yes/No. Three Dark Triad personas (Psychopathy, Machiavellianism, Narcissism) and two Moral Nihilism personas. Extra high-prior concepts: Interest in Science, Interest in Music, Desire to Create Allies, Machiavellianism.
- Context: chat-formatted user/assistant exchanges.
- Shot grid: 25 values from N = 0 to 128. A grid up to 320 appears in the Fig. 6 axis.
- Magnitudes: 29 values from -10 to +10.
- Sampling and fitting: 100 random sequences per cell; 725 averaged points per dataset-model pair.
- Models: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, Gemma-2-9B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, all 4-bit quantised.
- Steering method: Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA, difference in means) at a single best layer. quote: "For Llama-3.1-8B, this is consistently layer 12, for Gemma-2-9B, it is layer 20, and for Qwen-2.5-7B, it is layer 14."
- Metric: probability of the persona-matching token.

LIMITS
- Concede (p8): "One limitation of this work is that we only consider binary concepts and use only one method for constructing steering vectors (CAA)."
- Concede: larger and more capable LLMs are future work. Only models up to 70B were tested, all quantised to 4 bits.
- Steering had no clear effect on phi-4-mini-instruct.
- Steering only works in one or a few layers.
- The model is fit to averages over 100 sequences, not to individual outputs.
- Four parameters are fitted per dataset and model. Of these, a, b and gamma are not read off the model's priors, so this is a fit and not a first-principles prediction. The paper says so: the steering vector is not the "true" concept vector, and the prior b is estimated.
- The ICL labels are all concept-consistent, so the mismatched-label likelihood term reduces to -N. Mixed or contradictory demonstrations are not tested.
- The "unified" claim covers persona adoption plus one flipped-label task. System prompts, instructions, and persona prompts written as text are not tested. The only context type tested is many-shot Q/A exemplars.
- The paper tests no prompt-based persona or system prompt, no instruction-following task, no reasoning model, and no frontier model.
- Mechanism (how belief is implemented in the layers, and the likelihood function) is left open.
- Author concession: whether belief is represented non-linearly outside the linear subspace is unknown.

BUILDS ON
- Xie et al. 2021 (ICL as implicit Bayesian inference); Bigelow et al. 2023; Wurgaft et al. 2025 (source of the sub-linear discount tau); Arora et al. 2024 (Bayesian scaling laws for ICL); Panwar et al. 2024.
- Anil et al. 2024 (many-shot jailbreaking and its power-law scaling); Agarwal et al. 2024 (many-shot ICL; flipped-label task).
- Turner et al. 2024 and Panickssery et al. 2024 (CAA); Park et al. 2024b and 2025b (linear representation hypothesis); Elhage et al. 2022; Arditi et al. 2024 (refusal direction); Chen et al. 2025 (persona vectors).
- Goodman et al. 2008 (rule-based concept likelihood); Perez et al. 2022 (persona datasets); Malo et al. 2014 (financial phrasebank).

CODE: none in the paper. It implements steering with the open-source `steering-vectors` repository (footnote 2). The model equations above are the load-bearing part.

FIGURES
- Fig. 6, p7. "In-context learning and activation steering jointly affect behavior. The in-context learning dynamics we observe in Fig. 4 and the steering vector magnitude response function in Fig. 5 interact to create a phase boundary (Top). Our belief dynamics model re-constructs this diagram with high fidelity (Bottom)." Best single figure: it shows shots against steering magnitude as a heatmap, with the model reproducing the boundary.
- Fig. 4, p5. "In-context learning dynamics are sigmoidal with respect to N^(1-alpha) and modulated by activation steering." It explains the sudden-learning curve and the leftward shift under steering.
- Fig. 1, p2 is the conceptual overview.

FIT TO TARGET NOTE (01-how-models-read-prompts.md): the section on in-context examples and priming. The finding is that shots accumulate evidence and a persona/priming prior shifts the starting odds. Do not stretch it to system prompts or text personas, which the paper did not test.

PROBLEMS: Figure panels extracted as glyph garbage (axis labels unreadable), so values and curve shapes come from captions and text only. Reference list only skimmed. No embedded instructions found in the text.
